paper.title: ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities
paper.central_claim: A strategy of design principles for prompt engineering plus a high-level function library lets ChatGPT adapt to different robotics tasks, simulators and form factors, with the user on the loop; ChatGPT can be effective at several such tasks. (Also ships PromptCraft and an AirSim-ChatGPT tool; claim_type fixed by the self-stated central claim, anchors v2 item 3.)

evidence.quote: We outline a strategy that combines design principles for prompt engineering and the creation of a high-level function library which allows ChatGPT to adapt to different robotics tasks, simulators, and form factors.
We show that ChatGPT can be effective at solving several of such tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Effectiveness claim with no quantitative metric.

evidence.quote: most of the existing approaches are restricted by a rigid scope and limited set of functionalities, or by their open-loop nature that does not allow for fluid interactions and behavior corrections from user feedback
Previous approaches that rely on GPT-3 or Codex models [ 15 , 14 ] require the user to re-engineer the input prompt and generate new outputs from scratch.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed advantage of dialogue correction over re-prompting; not compared experimentally.

evidence.quote: The user stays on the loop to evaluate code output by ChatGPT, either through direct analysis or through simulation, and provides feedback to ChatGPT on the quality and safety of the output code
which leads to a unbounded text-based answer
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative contrast: no API guidance (Appendix A.1).

evidence.quote: API under-specification, which leads to hallucinations over function call parameters
Most of the examples we presented in this work demonstrated open perception-action loops where ChatGPT generated code to solve a task, with no feedback was provided to the model afterwards.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors admit most examples are open-loop.

evidence.quote: We emphasize that these tools should not be given full control of the robotics pipeline, especially for safety-critical applications.

We verify that the model is able to complete simple navigation tasks, but more research is needed in terms of properly describing the scene context in textual or vector form for more complex tasks and environments.
evidence.support_explanation: Only closed-loop dialogue example; qualitative, simple tasks.

evidence.quote: ChatGPT built most of the key building blocks for the avoidance algorithm, but required some human feedback on steps it missed
We also used ChatGPT with a different API implementation to control a real drone.
evidence.support_explanation: Real drone demo, no trial counts.

evidence.quote: ChatGPT was asked to learn the simpler skills of picking up objects, and then placing them.
evidence.support_explanation: In-conversation skill composition; persistence only within dialogue context.

evidence.quote: Prompt engineering is a mostly empirical science
evidence.support_explanation: Authors characterize the principles as empirical heuristics.

evidence.quote: A more structured response can be produced by requesting the model to use XML tags to help us parse the output automatically
evidence.support_explanation: Output structuring for parsing and clarification questions.

evidence.quote: is the conversational ability of our LLM, which allows the user to interactively improve and correct the robot
evidence.support_explanation: Stated difference to prior LLM-robotics work.

signatures.object: high-level robot function library (descriptively named wrappers over perception/motion APIs) plus structured task prompt
signatures.information: Prompt lists allowed functions, constraints, environment, state, goal and examples; ChatGPT sees nothing else; user sees code and optional simulation
signatures.operation: ChatGPT writes code chaining API calls; user inspects/simulates and replies with textual feedback; final code deployed
signatures.conditions: API names must be descriptive; under-specified APIs cause hallucinated parameters; no API guidance gives unbounded text
signatures.feedback: human textual feedback in dialogue; sometimes simulator/video
signatures.selection_rule_data: user decides acceptance; no automatic selection
signatures.persistence: functions defined earlier in the conversation reused later (in-context only)
signatures.claimed_effect: zero-shot task solutions across drones, arms, navigation
signatures.failure_boundary: open-loop, safety needs human, hallucination when APIs under-specified

signatures.object: dialogue-as-control-loop for navigation (Habitat): observations as polar-coordinate text each step, output restricted to move/turn
signatures.information: List of visible objects with distance/angle; commands limited to turn(angle), move(distance)
signatures.operation: ChatGPT emits one command per step; environment returns new text observation
signatures.conditions: simple tasks; scene description design left open
signatures.failure_boundary: complex tasks/environments need better scene description

signatures.object: XML-tagged response format (question/reason/command) for parsing and clarification
signatures.information: Prompt-specified tags and example clarification dialogue
signatures.operation: model asks clarifying question when ambiguous, otherwise outputs command

gap.author_gap: Existing LLM-robotics approaches have rigid scope or open-loop prompting that cannot take fluid user correction; re-prompting from scratch is needed with GPT-3/Codex.
gap.checked_gap: Real but coarse and asserted: no measurement shows the cost of re-prompting or the benefit of dialogue correction. Nearest neighbours (SayCan, Code as Policies, Socratic Models, Inner Monologue-type works) are cited, not compared or fetched.

lineage_closest_adjacent.name: Code as Policies / Codex-based code generation (refs 14, 15)
SayCan (ref 31)
lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: value-grounded action ranking in a fixed library
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved: open-ended code and multiple form factors

gap.residue: No quantitative evidence on success rates, failure frequency, robustness of design principles or cost; most examples open-loop with human in the loop.
gap.stakes: Authors motivate non-technical users deploying robots through language; stakes (safety, reliability) acknowledged but unmeasured.
gap.method_response: API library design + prompt structure + dialogue feedback + PromptCraft sharing platform.
gap.remaining_gap: Everything quantitative: success rates, closed-loop reliability, comparison with baselines, model/robot generality.
unresolved: Claimed benefit over GPT-3/Codex re-prompting not tested.
Closest neighbours not pinned locally; no novelty search.

claims.text: With a high-level function library and prompt-engineering principles ChatGPT can solve a range of robotics tasks zero-shot and adapt across form factors.
claims.setting: selected transcripts: basketball visual servoing, real Tello drone, AirSim inspection/obstacle avoidance, pick-stack-logo manipulation, AirSim object navigation, Habitat dialogue navigation
claims.selection_vs_test: authors choose and iterate prompts on the shown tasks; no held-out tasks
claims.allowed_conclusion: Existence demonstrations that ChatGPT can emit plausible API-calling code and respond to feedback; no rate of success, no reliability claim.

claims.text: API guidance matters: without it output is unbounded text; under-specified APIs cause hallucinated parameters.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Qualitative transcripts and video demos; no counted closed-loop trials (EVIDENCE.md: demos are not counted).
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors show curated ChatGPT transcripts in which API-calling code is produced and corrected by a human in the loop; this supports 'plausible in several settings', not a measured effectiveness, reliability or generality.
unresolved: closed-loop only in simple Habitat dialogue

G.reason: Genuine limitation (rigid scope, open-loop, re-prompting) but asserted rather than measured; nearest neighbours cited, not compared; remaining gap lists no boundary conditions.

M.reason: Design principles (descriptive API names, constraints, state, examples, tags) are plausible and illustrated by prompt-variant contrasts, but remain heuristic ('mostly empirical') with no distinguishable predictions against naive prompting.

X.reason: Pipeline steps and prompts are given (Appendix B) but conditions of validity, human role and failure handling are loosely specified; most examples open-loop; dialogue-as-controller only for simple navigation.

measurement.reason: No success rates, trial counts or baselines; demos judged by authors/videos.
